intent: Deliberately leave the current optional item of a Questionnaire unanswered and move on.
typical_uses: The way past an optional question the user declines to answer

dont_use_when.situation: An action button outside a questionnaire

invariants.text: `variant` and `size` are passed to the kit Button the component renders by default; when `render` is given it replaces that Button and both are ignored.
It is hidden whenever the current item is required. While hidden it carries the native `hidden` and `inert` attributes, `aria-hidden` and tabIndex -1, and `data-hidden` in place of `data-visible`.
Skipping clears the item's answer, sets its status to `skipped` so it submits nothing, and moves to the next item; on the last item it submits the form instead.

anti_patterns.dont: Use QuestionnaireSkip to move past a required item
anti_patterns.do_instead: Mark the item optional in both `items` and QuestionnaireItem; a required item has no skip path

a11y.by: questionnaire.test.tsx asserts Skip has the hidden property on a required item, and that a skipped item is absent from the submitted FormData

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the button's own state (`QuestionnaireNavigationState`: disabled, shortcut, status, visible), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted. The kit defaults it to its own Button.

good.title: A ghost Skip button with its own text

bad.title: Skip mounted only for optional items
bad.why: Skip already hides itself on a required item; a hand-written condition repeats state the root reads from `items` and drifts from it when the two disagree.

render.description: TS: RenderProp<QuestionnaireNavigationState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies.
